name: Drought
value: Sudan harvest hit; no famine declared
summary: El Niño drought cuts Sudan's harvest and raises famine risk; no drought famine declaration or exporter harvest failure
state: July–September rainfall in Sudan was the lowest in more than three decades, with North Darfur the driest since 1984, and the IPC warned on 12 Oct of rising famine risk in conflict areas (Reuters via TimesLIVE, 23 Oct). GEOGLAM's Crop Monitor of 5 Nov reports drought hampering wheat emergence in southern and central Europe and hurting crops in Mexico and Thailand, but no outright harvest failure. Severe drought in a major crop region keeps Watch; no new drought-driven famine declaration or major exporter harvest failure was found as of 17 Nov.
for_you: Households in drought-hit parts of Sudan face the most acute risk. Elsewhere, effects tend to show up later through food prices; ample global grain stocks have so far limited that.
rubric_hit: Severe drought in a major crop region (Sudan; southern Europe emergence) = Watch; no famine or exporter failure

sources.title: TimesLIVE (Reuters) — New famine risk haunts war-torn Sudan with El Niño-driven drought
GEOGLAM — Crop Monitor for AMIS, November 2026

why: Drought slowly destroys harvests, hydropower and river shipping, and drives famine and migration.
drivers: Rainfall deficits, heat, ENSO, groundwater depletion.

rubric.alert: Drought driving famine conditions, a major exporter's harvest failure, or monsoon failure across a major breadbasket.
rubric.watch: Severe drought in a major crop region, a major river at record low, or a monsoon running more than 20% below normal.
rubric.normal: No major breadbasket in severe drought.
